primary_sources: AWS Serverless Best Practices & Lambda Guidelines

rules.explanation: Tying microservices together using synchronous HTTP REST calls creates cascading failures and tight service coupling during partial outages.
rules.do: Implement asynchronous, event-driven communication using message brokers and event buses (e.g., AWS SQS, SNS, Kafka) for decoupled service interactions.
rules.dont: Do not build complex chains of synchronous HTTP service dependencies that cause system-wide downtime if a single downstream service fails.

rules.rule_name: Serverless Cold Start Optimization and Function Granularity
rules.explanation: Packing heavy monolithic codebases into serverless function handlers drastically increases cold start latency and resource over-provisioning.
rules.do: Keep serverless functions lightweight, single-purpose (Single Responsibility Principle), and optimize package sizes to minimize cold start delays.
rules.dont: Do not deploy monolithic applications inside serverless function runtimes or bundle unnecessary dependencies into function deployment packages.

rules.explanation: Debugging requests flowing across dozens of distributed serverless functions or microservices without unified tracing is extremely difficult.
rules.do: Integrate distributed tracing frameworks (e.g., AWS X-Ray, OpenTelemetry) and centralized log aggregation across all service boundaries.
rules.dont: Do not rely on isolated local log files scattered across independent microservice instances for debugging production errors.

rules.rule_name: Idempotent Event Processing and Failure Retries
rules.explanation: Failing to design event handlers to be idempotent leads to duplicate data processing and corrupted database states during automatic retry storms.
rules.do: Ensure all serverless and microservice event consumers implement idempotent processing logic using unique transaction IDs or state tracking.
rules.dont: Do not assume message brokers will deliver events strictly once without accounting for duplicate retries.
